precepts.text: It is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; his tribe is reckoned from his father, as every Israelite's is.
precepts.point: Our Lord sprang out of Judah, and the tribe comes from the father.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.” The children are the disciples, us, and Christ took part of the same flesh and blood. “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham”, which is flesh and blood. “Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” In all things, not some things. How is a man made like his brethren in all things? By having a father and a mother.

Then Hebrews 7: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.” He sprang out of Judah based on his father. The tribe comes from the father, as every Israelite’s does.

The fathers show the same. God told David, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels.” David knew “that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne.” And Paul says Christ “was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.” According to the flesh: made flesh and blood like his brethren.

That is why Matthew says “When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” Coming together was the customary wedding feast, as when Laban “made a feast” and Jacob went in unto his wife. Joseph and Mary were already espoused, and betrothal is marriage, so there was no fornication; they lay together before the feast. Child of the Holy Ghost means child of prophecy, the prophecy made to David. Joseph, a just man, was “not willing to make her a publick example”, which means stoned to death, and “was minded to put her away privily”: to hide her, because the child was his. Why would a just man hide a woman for something he did not do? And the angel called him “Joseph, thou son of David.” So our Lord sprang out of Judah through his father, made like his brethren in all things.

precepts.text: The priests under the law were many, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death; but this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. That is how Christ is able to save to the uttermost and atone continually: there is no death in him.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The day of atonement, when Israel was to “afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord”, is a representation of Christ. Christ was that atonement.

“By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.” The better testament is the new covenant. “And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death”: the priests under the law died, one after another.

“But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him”. Christ is the true high priest, with no death in him. That is how he is able to atone for our sins continually, where the old priests could only atone until they died.

precepts.text: A disannulling of the commandment for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof, for the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope, Christ, did: the annulled commandment is sacrifice.
precepts.point: Ye who were kept under the law are all the children of God by faith in Christ, whether Jew or Greek, bond or free, male or female, the same people in different conditions. If ye be Christ's then are ye Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise, and the promise pertains to Israel; name me one other nation God calls his people in the Old Testament.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” What commandment was annulled? Sacrifice. It was annulled for its weakness and unprofitableness, done away in Christ. That is the same weakness as Romans 8:3, the law that was weak through the flesh.

“For the law made nothing perfect”. What law made nothing perfect? Hebrews 10:1 said the sacrifices offered could not make the comers thereunto perfect. It made no man perfect. “but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.” Not what, but who: Christ is the better hope, and through him we draw nigh unto God.

That is why “after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster”. The schoolmaster, the law of sacrifice, was disannulled, and the ye who were kept under it, whether called Jews or Greeks, bond or free, male or female, are the same people of God in Christ.

“And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” The promise pertains to the Israelites. All nations are not the children of promise. If they are, name the nation God calls his people in the old covenant. Isaiah 19 says Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands, but Isaiah 27, Isaiah 11 and Zechariah 10 show that means the children of Israel gathered out of Egypt and Assyria. That is called precepts.

precepts.text: It is evident that our Lord sprang out of Judah, of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood. Christ from Judah is the lawgiver.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.
precepts.why:
Psalm 60 says “Judah is my lawgiver”, when you would expect it to say Levi. Hebrews gives the reason: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

So Christ is the lawgiver. He comes from the tribe of Judah, and he is the one that gave Moses the laws. That is the Lord Isaiah speaks of: “the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” Our judge, our lawgiver and our king is Christ out of Judah, and it is he who will save us when the warships and navies of the nations come down.

precepts.text: There is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof, for the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did, by the which we draw nigh unto God. Hebrews 10:1: the law, having a shadow of good things to come, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. Animal sacrifice is the weak and beggarly elements, unprofitable because we were too sinful to keep maintaining it.
precepts.point: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years; I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. Colossians 2:16: let no man judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. Ezekiel 45:17 answers both: it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings, and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths, and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and the Pharisees, whose bread and butter was people bringing animals, were trying to win the churches back to temple law, saying to hell with what Christ did. If you need an animal, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Paul calls them “weak and beggarly elements”. Hebrews calls the same thing weak: “For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” The disannulling is of animal sacrifice. What made it weak and unprofitable? “For the law made nothing perfect”, including the man's conscience, “but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.” That better hope is Christ.

Hebrews 10 says it again: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” It could not make those who offered them perfect.

So the weak and beggarly elements are the sacrificing of animals. They were unprofitable because we were too sinful to keep maintaining them.

That is why verse 10 says “Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years”. Ezekiel 45:17 shows that it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. Colossians 2:16 matches it: meat, drink, holyday, new moon and sabbath days: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and Christ is the body, the sacrifice for all of those things. The Galatians were turning back to observing those days by the weak and beggarly elements.

precepts.text: Such an high priest, holy, harmless, undefiled, who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
precepts.point: Aaron dipped his finger in the blood and put it upon the horns of the altar, burnt the fat and kidneys and caul, the guts, upon the altar, and the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire without the camp; you keep reading it over and over, without the camp.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

precepts.why:
The priest had to make an atonement for himself first, and then offer the offering of the people. Hebrews opens up that order: “such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people’s: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.”

Aaron slew the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself, before the people’s. Christ, the high priest after the order of Melchisedec, is holy, harmless, and undefiled, and had no sins of his own to atone for; he offered up himself once.

precepts.text: The priesthood being changed, there is a change also of the law; it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda.
precepts.point: When Christ died the veil of the temple was rent and the priesthood was changed; the high priest now is Christ, for it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda. The sons of Levi no longer carry that office; Judah carries this work to the kingdom.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

precepts.why:
“For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.” The high priest of Leviticus 21 was of the sons of Aaron, of the tribe of Levi. But “he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar. For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

The high priest now is Christ, out of Juda. The sons of Levi no longer carry that office; Judah carries this work to the kingdom.

precepts.text: Our Lord sprang out of Juda, of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood; no man of another tribe gave attendance at the altar.
precepts.point: Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

note.label: Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest’s office, “and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.” Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

Paul shows the same law still standing in his day: “For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar. For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

Christ sprang out of Juda, and no man of that tribe gave attendance at the altar, because Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood for any tribe but Levi. Even the Lord’s own tribe was a stranger to the priest’s office under this law; only Aaron and his sons waited on it.
